The ledger L4 cells therefore stay at the cycle they were last worked; the CallFrom, Memo and Multicall3From reading on Arc and the ConfigurableAccount precompile on Tempo after T14 (L-105) are the parts that the coming forks or this cycle's reading make stale.

theme-celo-xlayer-arc-journal-lift ran the frame journal of arc-node v0.8.6 (1,062 sequences) but not the second revert protocol that the subcall precompile uses. In crates/evm/src/evm.rs at v0.8.6 (fetched by the critic), init_subcall takes checkpoint() and at once checkpoint_commit() (lines 1052-1053), and complete_subcall rolls back a child that succeeded through revert_subcall_checkpoint, a dummy checkpoint followed by checkpoint_revert(saved_cp) (lines 1249-1259), when completion accounting runs out of gas (1186-1196) or completion fails (1226-1228). The cleared items on CallFrom read the main branch for sender spoofing and transient sharing only; none ran the rollback with PoolManager state inside the child. The verifier of the theme raised the same question at medium.

The TIP-1060 credit region of the v1.19.2 SSTORE handler and the SLOAD miss path are still unrun from the binary (L-1318 inconclusive for the second cycle); cycle 37 ran the credit branch live with the credit word overridden, which tests the running node but not the binary model. Separately, the evm2 revision 7c9f3b6 that Tempo pins carries an entry for a transaction dispatched from inside a running one (suspended_frames, enclosing_refund, ExecutionGuard in evm/mod.rs, cycle 32 critic). OPCODES.md says no Tempo code calls it today, but no unit has read what it does with transient storage and the journal, so its effect on A1 is unknown before T15 is tagged.

An earlier clearance of Tempo's native branch said the zero balance was confirmed for probe accounts and not for every genesis account. The critic fetched crates/chainspec/src/genesis/presto.json from tempoxyz/tempo main (chainId 4217, the file PRESTO loads in crates/chainspec/src/spec.rs:140-142): 14 alloc entries, none with a nonzero balance. eth_getProof on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz returns balance 0x0 for the PoolManager 0x33620f62…7029, for address 0x0 and for 0xfeec…0000, while eth_getBalance answers the 0x4242… placeholder. The placeholder is an RPC answer, not trie state. What is still unread is whether any system call or precompile on Tempo credits a native balance after genesis.

The official endpoints of Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM and Arc still refuse eth_simulateV1 (cycle 37 profiles), so the 23 multi-transaction scenarios and stalesync.py have run on these networks only through third-party endpoints or a replica (Arc on PublicNode, Monad and MegaETH on cycle 35 endpoints) or not at all (HyperEVM).

F-118 says no public RPC node re-executes MegaETH blocks, while the high-throughput profile for 4326 L2 says the public stateless validator reproduced all 23 PoolManager blocks from 32,983,020 to 32,994,402. Both can be true (the validator is not an RPC node), but F-118's wording now reads as if nothing re-executes the producer's blocks; it was last verified in cycle 24 and should be restated against the validator evidence of cycles 35 to 37.

Jenner, Salvador and Tempo T14 fall on 8 December 2026, T15 targets 15 December, and Lagoon activates on 11 January 2027. Every cycle is dated 2026-11-27, so L-545, L-1032, L-1075, L-1224 and the T15 watch can only be answered after those dates. Cycle 37 reread the schedules and nothing else can be done on them now.

leads.question: On arc-node v0.8.6 (and on the drpc v0.8.6 endpoint that serves eth_simulateV1 or eth_call with overrides), give an EOA an EIP-7702 designator by state override that points to an unlock callback contract, then from that EOA call Multicall3From so that CallFrom calls PoolManager.unlock with the EOA as sender. Inside the callback do a take of an ERC-20 and of native USDC, a settle, a swap and an ERC-6909 mint, and a nested Multicall3From call from the callback. Choose the outer gas so that the child returns success and complete_subcall then runs out of gas (evm.rs 1186-1196). After the precompile reports failure, are every PoolManager slot (slot0, liquidity, ticks, positions, ERC-6909 balances), every token balance, the native balance, the 0x3600 face and the transient Lock, delta and count slots back to their values before the subcall?
leads.why: This rollback is hand built (checkpoint then immediate commit at evm.rs 1052-1053, later a dummy checkpoint and checkpoint_revert at 1249-1259) and is not revm's frame revert that the journal lifts tested. If it restored PoolManager storage but kept a token transfer, or restored the debit but not the payout, an ordinary account could keep a take whose debt was rolled back, which drains any pool on Arc. Settlement relies on all of src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 and 291-297 reverting together.

leads.question: Using the mega-evm and SALT sources that F-105 cites, at what bucket multiplier does one zero to nonzero SSTORE cost more than the per-transaction gas limit, the per-transaction storage gas or state growth limit, or the block limits that apply to transactions sent through the sequencer, and what does an ordinary account pay to grow one bucket that far under the 80 percent doubling rule? Is there any cap on bucket growth or any shrink rule that runs without the operator?
leads.why: F-105 stops at the L1 exit, which closes at multiplier 64 for about 0.003 ETH. Position.update writes two fee growth slots on every liquidity change (src/libraries/Position.sol:99-100), and a first token balance or a new tick is also a zero to nonzero write. If the sequencer limit can be reached at a cost below the value of the targeted positions, an ordinary account can freeze chosen LP positions on MegaETH for good, which is an in-scope freeze.

leads.question: For the 137 PoolManager positions with liquidity on MegaETH, which ones need a zero to nonzero write on their next removal through the sequencer (fee growth slots, a recipient's first token balance, an ERC-6909 first balance) and which can avoid it, and what share of the PoolManager's value sits in those that cannot?
leads.why: Sizes the impact of the previous lead and of F-105 before anyone tests the cost of bucket growth.

leads.question: The cycle 37 census says PoolManager pc 22445 and 22513 (the wide fee mulDiv in SwapMath) have never run in a HyperEVM block and are reachable in existing pools with amountSpecified of -2^236 or below, and that the swap consumes only what the price limit allows. On a HyperEVM replica, with the deployed PoolManager, does eth_call of such a swap against an existing pool return an amount that can be settled, and how much does it move? Then, does Hyperliquid's documentation or any hl-node release note say that the producer compiles or caches code per contract or per program counter?
leads.why: If those sites are reachable with a settleable amount, the only evidence for them on the producer is shape coverage in other contracts. A producer that specialises per contract would leave the PoolManager's own wide branch untested, and a wrong result there changes the input left after fees in src/libraries/SwapMath.sol for every pool.

leads.question: L-875 is parked: is there now any public method on mainnet.megaeth.com (realtime or mega_ namespace, eth_sendRawTransactionSync dry runs, eth_estimateGas forwarded to the sequencer) whose answer comes from the sequencer's JIT rather than the replica's interpreter? If one exists, run the BYTE, SAR and SIGNEXTEND vectors on which the evmone-compiler handlers are wrong (F-166).
leads.why: Mined blocks show the producer gives the specified result at every PoolManager site it has run. A JIT path reachable through a public method would test the sites it has not run, and would be the only way to see a future producer build before it writes state.

leads.question: Does any Tempo system call, precompile or fee path credit a native balance after genesis (for example a mint to a system address at block start, a refund in native units, or a test-only path left on in the mainnet chainspec)? Check with eth_getProof on the system addresses that the block executor calls and on the fee manager.
leads.why: The presto genesis holds no native balance and eth_getProof shows 0x0 for the PoolManager. A single funded account would let native credit be minted with real value calls and spent against address(0) pools that hold single sided ERC-20 liquidity, so the clearance rests on there being none.

leads.question: Do any address(0) pools exist on the Tempo PoolManager, and does any of them hold ERC-20 liquidity in a single sided range?
leads.why: Bounds the previous lead: if no such pool holds ERC-20 liquidity, a native credit has nothing to buy.

leads.question: In arc-node v0.8.6, does the subcall continuation map keyed by frame depth (evm.rs 217-218, 1081-1090, 757-758) stay correct when a child at depth d+1 makes its own CallFrom subcall through a 7702 delegated tx.origin, when the child halts with CallTooDeep, and when an inspector is attached as on the tracing node? Could a continuation stored for one depth be taken by a different frame that finishes at the same depth?
leads.why: A continuation taken by the wrong frame would apply the wrong rollback checkpoint, which can leave a PoolManager payout in place after its debit was reverted. The nesting is reachable by any account whose own EOA runs delegated code.

leads.question: Does Multicall3From in contracts/src/batch/Multicall3From.sol at v0.8.6 pass msg.sender as the sender to CallFrom on every path (aggregate, tryAggregate, value paths), so that a contract called by a victim EOA cannot ask for tx.origin as sender?
leads.why: The EVM check in init_subcall allows the sender to be the helper or tx.origin (evm.rs 959-968). If Multicall3From let any caller name tx.origin, every contract a user calls on Arc could move that user's ERC-6909 claims and approvals at the PoolManager (src/ERC6909.sol). Memo passes msg.sender (Memo.sol:43); Multicall3From was read on main only.

leads.question: Run the out-of-line CALLDATALOAD path of compiled block 0xde6 with calldata shorter than 68 bytes from the shipped gcc build of Monad 0.16.7 (cycle 37 lead), and also with calldata of exactly 4, 35 and 36 bytes.
leads.why: The last part of the compiled clear block that has not run. A wrong word there changes the amount compared at src/PoolManager.sol:314.

leads.question: Is there a mined OP Mainnet or Zora block in which a deposit transaction with value failed and a PoolManager transaction follows in the same block, and does its trace show the mint landing at the deposit's from address and the transient state of the next transaction empty?
leads.why: Failed deposits were read in source only. The PoolManager credits native only from msg.value, so the question is a confirmation of A1 at the deposit boundary, not a new credit path.

leads.question: Lift the inlined checkpoint and commit from make_call_frame and frame_return in the celo-reth v1.0.10, xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 and arc-node v0.8.6 binaries and run them on the PoolManager reentry sequences, as the theme did for the EvmInternals copies.

leads.question: Do Base B20 token policies park a transfer that fails the receiver policy in a guard contract, as Tempo's receive policy does (F-033), or do they revert?
leads.why: Transfer of F-033: a take that succeeds while the funds are parked costs the taker, and a parked amount that later returns to the PoolManager would be surplus a settler could book. Token sweep beyond this one question is out of the cycle's focus.

leads.question: Which EVM changes does the Lagoon (Upgrade 22) release of op-reth carry besides the interop predeploys: any opcode, precompile repricing, gas cap per transaction or change to deposit handling? Read the op-reth release that schedules 1799683201.
leads.why: The cycle 37 profiles name Lagoon as the only fork and checked its predeploys. A change to an opcode handler or to the transaction gas cap would change what pool math or a long swap returns from 11 January 2027.
